HS Classification V2 Target Architecture
nodes.rationale: Transforms a frontend-only LLM classifier (105 hardcoded BTKI entries, no audit trail) into a database-centric system with 14,273 BTKI entries, 65,833 EN paragraphs and full source traceability; classification becomes fact extraction -> database retrieval -> rules engine -> validation instead of direct LLM prediction, eliminating hallucination risk.

nodes.label: Principle: Database as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: All HS codes, descriptions and legal guidance must come from the database, never from LLM memory, so a wrong or invented code is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

nodes.label: Principle: Sequential KUM HS 1-6 Application
nodes.rationale: Customs classification is legally defined by the WCO General Rules for Interpretation applied in order; applying them out of order or skipping to a code produces an indefensible result under Indonesian BTKI 2022.

nodes.label: Principle: Auditability to Source Document
nodes.rationale: Every classification decision must be traceable to file, page and paragraph of the original ruling document so customs professionals can defend it in an audit or dispute.

nodes.label: Principle: Validation-First Release Gate
nodes.rationale: No result is released without code existence, parent hierarchy and source ID confirmation; a result that fails validation is never shown to the user, which converts a silent hallucination into a visible error.

nodes.label: Principle: Ask, Don't Guess
nodes.rationale: When discriminator facts are missing the system must ask a targeted question instead of defaulting to a generic .00 code; defaulting silently misclassifies goods and hides uncertainty from the user.

nodes.label: Admin Data Center
nodes.rationale: Isolates all trust-boundary data ingestion (DOCX parsing, template upload, validation, versioning) from the runtime classification path so bad nomenclature data cannot reach production queries.

nodes.label: DOCX Parser Module (IDocxParser)
nodes.rationale: OOXML structure signals (w:pStyle, w:outlineLvl, w:numPr, w:ind, w:tbl) are the only reliable carrier of BTKI hierarchy in the source Word file; when a parent cannot be determined the parser flags STRUCTURE_AMBIGUITY and routes to human review instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Template Ingestion Module (ITemplateIngestion)
nodes.rationale: Provides a CSV/Excel escape hatch for manual corrections and partial updates when DOCX parsing is impractical; DOCX parse takes precedence over template rows so a later authoritative import wins.

nodes.label: Nomenclature Import State Machine
nodes.rationale: Explicit states (UPLOADED -> PARSING -> MAPPED -> VALIDATING -> DRY_RUN_* -> READY_TO_COMMIT -> COMMITTED -> INDEXED -> ACTIVE) force a dry run before commit so a partial or broken dataset can never be marked ACTIVE.

nodes.label: Dry Run Validation Before Commit
nodes.rationale: Checks parent existence, duplicates, circular references, date overlap and expected counts (14,273 lines) before COMMIT, because a bad activated nomenclature version corrupts every subsequent classification.

nodes.label: Fact Extraction Engine (IFactExtractor)
nodes.rationale: Splits objective evidence gathering from legal reasoning: the LLM may read free text and normalize units but must never infer a missing fact, because an invented weight or material silently drives the whole downstream classification.

nodes.label: FactStatus (UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE/ZERO/CONFLICTING/VERIFIED)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes 'not provided' from 'genuinely zero' and 'not relevant'; collapsing these into null is what causes systems to default a missing weight to a generic subheading.

nodes.label: Information Gain Question Prioritization
nodes.rationale: Ordering questions by (CandidatesEliminated / TotalCandidates) x FactReliability minimizes the number of questions a user must answer; gains are recalculated after each answer because the candidate set shrinks.

nodes.label: Candidate Generation Engine (ICandidateGenerator)
nodes.rationale: Eight retrieval strategies (lexical, synonym mapping, multilingual, semantic embeddings, function, material, legal-note referral, EN cross-reference) are combined because no single search finds the right heading for both 'laptop' and 'crane barge'.

nodes.label: CandidateHeading (Enriched Candidate)
nodes.rationale: Candidates are enriched with applicable section/chapter/subheading notes, EN paragraphs, required discriminators, parent hierarchy and source_id at retrieval time so the rules engine never needs a second DB round trip mid-reasoning.

nodes.label: KUM HS 1: Heading + Notes + EN
nodes.rationale: Heading text alone is never determinative: section notes, chapter notes and EN exclusions/inclusions can eliminate or refer a candidate, so they are applied inside rule 1 before any specificity comparison.

nodes.label: KUM HS 3(a): Specific vs General Heading
nodes.rationale: Specificity is scored (specific article +1.0, residual 'other' -1.0, complete vs parts +/-0.5, material coverage +0.5/-0.3) so the comparison is reproducible and its evidence can be recorded in the reasoning chain.

nodes.label: KUM HS 3(c): Last in Numerical Order
KUM HS 6: Subheading Descent
nodes.rationale: Subheadings must be compared only against siblings at the same dash level (1-dash then 2-dash then 3-dash); comparing across levels or parent headings is legally invalid.

nodes.label: Essential Character Evaluation (Weighted Factors)
nodes.rationale: Weighs function/role 0.3, material 0.15, bulk 0.15, value 0.15, necessity 0.15 and consumer perception 0.1; no single factor is determinative, and when the factors are inconclusive the system escalates to expert review rather than picking a plausible heading.

nodes.label: Validation System (IValidator)
nodes.rationale: Six checks (code exists, format, parents exist, description exact match, code active on date, source_ids valid) form the last line of defence against a hallucinated code reaching a customs declaration.

nodes.label: Tariff Lookup Module (ITariffLookupModule)
nodes.rationale: Runs only after validation passes; FTA entitlement and PPN/PPh 22 rates carry mandatory disclaimers because rate availability is not the same as legal entitlement (rules of origin, PMK exemptions).

nodes.label: Source ID Format {document}:{checksum}:{part}:{location}
nodes.rationale: A single resolvable string (e.g. PMK26-2022:abc123def456:body:p150:table_5:row_42:cell_1) lets any decision be replayed back to the exact cell of the original Word document, which is what makes the audit trail defensible.

nodes.label: explanatory_notes Table (65,833 paragraphs)
nodes.rationale: EN paragraphs are stored with paragraph_type (SCOPE, DEFINITION, INCLUSION, EXCLUSION, TECHNICAL, EXAMPLE, BORDERLINE, CROSS_REFERENCE) and previous/next links so multi-paragraph exclusions survive segmentation without being truncated mid-statement.

nodes.label: Section / Chapter / Subheading Notes Tables
nodes.rationale: effect_type (DEFINITION, INCLUSION, EXCLUSION, CONDITION, REFERRAL, PRIORITY) plus target_codes/referred_codes makes notes machine-applicable rather than narrative text a model would have to interpret from memory.

nodes.label: nomenclature_versions Table
nodes.rationale: Only one version may be ACTIVE per effective date range; historical cases keep their version_id so a later reclassification never rewrites past decisions.

nodes.label: reasoning_events Table (Audit Trail)
nodes.rationale: Records candidates_before/after, decision and source_ids per applied rule; immutability is required even across version rollback and correction so the original reasoning can always be shown to an auditor.

nodes.label: Property 1: Source Traceability Completeness
nodes.rationale: Every extracted entity and retrieved candidate must carry a populated source_id; without it a decision cannot be defended and the auditability principle is unenforceable.

nodes.label: Property 2: No Hallucinated Codes or Descriptions
nodes.rationale: Any candidate or final code must exist as an exact match in btki_tariff_lines for the active version; this is the machine-checkable form of the no-hallucination guarantee.

nodes.label: Property 3: Fact Extraction Never Defaults
nodes.rationale: A missing fact must be UNKNOWN with a null value; defaulting would make a guess indistinguishable from evidence in the audit trail.

nodes.label: Property 20: Audit Trail Immutability
nodes.rationale: Reasoning events survive version rollback, expert review and correction; rewriting them would destroy the ability to show why a past declaration was made.

nodes.label: Property-Based Testing Strategy (FsCheck, 100 iterations)
nodes.rationale: The 20 correctness properties are universal claims over all inputs, so example-based tests cannot prove them; FsCheck at 100 iterations per property plus xUnit unit tests and Docker-backed integration tests cover the gap.

nodes.label: Gold Standard Test Cases (WEA08, WEA35, Laptop)
Error Handling and Recovery Strategy
nodes.rationale: Categorised recovery (import errors block activation, DB errors retry with backoff and circuit breaker, LLM errors degrade to keyword extraction) keeps a single component failure from producing a wrong classification; validation failure rate above 1% pages engineering.

nodes.label: Success Criteria (0 hallucination, >=95% gold standard, <=5s p90)
Non-Negotiable Principles (LLM cannot invent HS codes, descriptions, notes or EN)
nodes.rationale: The whole V2 system is designed so legal authority lives in the BTKI database, not in model weights; every code, description, note and EN must carry a source_id.

nodes.label: LLM Prohibited Actions
nodes.rationale: Final code selection, confidence and missing-fact guessing are removed from the LLM because they are the exact hallucination surfaces V1 suffered from.

nodes.label: LLM Permitted Actions (extraction, normalization, candidate ranking, KADL narrative)
Deterministic KUM HS Rules Engine
nodes.rationale: A deterministic engine is required so that every decision is reproducible and reconstructable from structured reasoning events, unlike a RAG-only chatbot.

nodes.label: Retrieval Engine (BTKI nodes, ancestors, notes, EN, cross-refs)
Validator (exact code, description, active-date, hierarchy, indent, source ID)
Fact Gate (UNKNOWN / NOT_APPLICABLE / ZERO / CONFLICTING / VERIFIED)
nodes.rationale: Empty fields must not be conflated with not-applicable, because that distinction changes which legal test can be run.

nodes.label: NEED_CLARIFICATION Response Contract
nodes.rationale: When a decisive fact is missing the system must stop and ask rather than guess; questions are ordered by information gain to eliminate candidates fastest.

nodes.label: Candidate Generation (lexical, semantic, function, material, note referral)
nodes.rationale: Semantic similarity is only allowed to produce candidates, never the final basis, because similarity is evidence not law.

nodes.label: KUM HS 1 (heading terms, Section Notes, Chapter Notes, EN assistance)
KUM HS 2(a) (incomplete, unfinished, unassembled, CKD/SKD, blank)
KUM HS 2(b) (mixtures and combinations of materials)
KUM HS 3(b) (essential character, retail set test)
KUM HS 5(b) (packing materials and packing containers)
KUM HS 6 (same-level subheading comparison after heading lock)
Heading Lock (single retained four-digit heading)
nodes.rationale: Once a heading is locked under GIR 1-5, later GIR 6 analysis must not reopen comparison against other headings, otherwise same-level comparison is violated.

nodes.label: Confidence Caps and Hard Failures
nodes.rationale: Caps exist because a high weighted score must never outrank a missing decisive fact; hierarchy or same-level violations return INVALID_RESULT instead of a low confidence.

nodes.label: Immutable Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Decisions must be reconstructable; structured legal reasoning and evidence are stored, never private chain-of-thought.

nodes.label: tariff_rate Table (MFN_BM, FTA_BM, PPN_IMPORT, PPH22_IMPORT)
nodes.rationale: FTA rates are stored per scheme/country alongside MFN so preference never overwrites the MFN record and multiple rates can apply to one code.

nodes.label: reasoning_event Table (hash-chained sequence)
nodes.rationale: previous_event_hash/event_hash make the reasoning chain tamper-evident so a decision can be reconstructed and audited later.

nodes.label: DOCX Ingestion Pipeline (OOXML-first, deterministic parser)
nodes.rationale: The BTKI and EN masters ship as Microsoft Word, so DOCX is the primary ingestion format; feeding whole Word documents to an LLM would break the no-invention rule.

nodes.label: OOXML Structure Mapping (styles, outline level, numbering, indentation, tables)
STRUCTURE_AMBIGUITY Review Queue
nodes.rationale: When code, dash, indentation and parent hierarchy disagree the parser must flag and queue the record rather than guess a parent.

nodes.label: DOCX Visual Verification Workflow (render, sample, side-by-side, reconcile, approve)
Tracked Changes and Non-Final Text Handling
nodes.rationale: Deleted text must never be silently merged into the active database; accepted view is used only after confirmation.

nodes.label: Import Pipeline State Machine (UPLOADED to ACTIVE)
Canonical vs Formatted Code Normalization (84713020 / 8471.30.20)
nodes.rationale: Codes are stored without dots as canonical form and leading zeros are preserved, because code identity must be byte-exact against the master.

nodes.label: Legal Note Category Clarification (no synthetic 'Catatan Pos')
nodes.rationale: Notes that target a heading keep their original source_type and gain target_heading; the UI may group them as 'Ketentuan Terkait Pos' without inventing a legal category.

nodes.label: Tariff Lookup Panel (MFN, FTA list, PPN, PPh 22, source, effective dates)
FTA Rate Reference vs FTA Eligibility Separation
nodes.rationale: A published preferential rate does not prove entitlement; origin, scheme, rules of origin, certificate and direct consignment still have to be satisfied.

nodes.label: KADL (Klasifikasi Atas Dasar Legal) Human Output
Security Controls (untrusted documents, tenant isolation, RBAC)
V2 Scope Boundary (lartas and PMK special treatment deferred)
nodes.rationale: Architecture separates classification result, standard tariff lookup, FTA reference and special regulatory/fiscal treatment so lartas and PMK rules can be added later without touching the classification engine.
